Order No. 09 Dated- 20.04.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Kurkura P.S. Case No. 02 of 2022 instituted under Sections 341/323/307/498A/504/34 of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

As per F.I.R., it appears that the petitioner is the husband of the opposite party no. 2 and she was abused to withdraw earlier case filed by her and on her refusal, she was assaulted by her in-laws with an intention to kill her.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
Earlier a Complaint Case No. 114 of 2021 was filed by the informant is still pending.

The informant was the sister-in-law (Bhabhi) of the petitioner and after death of her husband, informant's marriage was solemnized with the petitioner in a Temple Amreshwar Dham at Khunti on 18.06.2013, and out of their wedlock a female child was begotten.
There was matrimonial discard between the parties.

Although informant is still residing at her in-laws' house and the petitioner is providing her maintenance allowance as per order of this Court passed in earlier A.B.A.
No. 9129 of 2021.
The allegation of assault, torture and harassment has been falsely imputed against the petitioner with a view to harassing him.
The injury report of the informant shows only complain of pain on some part of body.

It is further submitted that petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case and will not indulge in tampering with prosecution evidence and will abide by all terms and conditions imposed by this Court in the matter of granting anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned A.P.P appearing for the State as well as Ms. Sunita Kumari, learned counsel appearing for the opposite party no. 2 have vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and has submitted that there is serious allegation against the petitioner and he has ruined the life of informant and also solemnized second marriage with another lady.

The informant was compelled to lodge second FIR on repeated physical assault and torture extended to her at the instance of petitioner and his family members and pressure created for withdrawal of case.
Petitioner has given false statements several times and also dare to deny the marriage with the informant and the paternity of the female child.
The petitioner is teacher but he poses himself to be a farmer.
The petitioner is also not complied with the under Section 41(A) CrPC.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner may not be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record, I feel inclined to extend privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Gumla, in connection with Kurkura P.S. Case No. 02 of 2022 with the condition that he will co-operate with the investigation of the case and appear before the investigating officer as and when noticed by him and furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Umesh/-
